functions.description: Run a write statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL).

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Run a read-only SQL query and return the result rows.

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Run a short worker-side pipeline in one call: each step triggers a function and its result lands in the next step's payload at `into` (default "/value") — large values flow worker→worker and never enter the chat. fp::* transform steps (get/pick/omit/take/drop/map/filter/split/join/uniq/size/compact/nth/getOr/flatten/sortBy/reverse/when, lodash semantics) run inline and thread the transformed value itself — the {value} wrapper they return when called directly never appears between steps. A failing fp::when guard STOPS the pipe (`short_circuited: true`), so a trailing write step runs only when its condition holds. The FIRST step receives no threaded value: start with a producing function (a fetch, a state::get) or seed a leading transform via payload.value. Example: fetch an article and persist it trimmed: through=[{function:'scrapling::fetch', payload:{url,format:'markdown'}}, {function:'fp::get', payload:{path:'/content'}}, {function:'fp::take', payload:{n:20000}}, {function:'state::set', payload:{scope,key}}]. Returns per-step sizes and a preview, not the value. shell::*/coder::* steps run under the session's harness-stamped filesystem scope; without one (no working directory, or a non-harness caller) they are refused — call them directly instead. Database write steps are refused only while `approval::gate` is registered.

into.description: JSON pointer in THIS step's payload where the previous step's value lands (default `/value`). Object keys only (`~0`/`~1` escapes are decoded); indexing into arrays is unsupported.

payload.description: Base payload for the call.

preview_chars.description: Preview length of the final threaded value in the receipt (capped at 8000).

through.description: Steps run in order; step N+1 receives step N's threaded value.

chars.description: Size of the value threaded OUT of this step (chars of its string or serialized form).

note.description: Set when the threaded value REPLACED a non-null literal already in this step's payload at the `into` pointer — almost always an omitted `into` on a write step clobbering the value it meant to write.

short_circuited.description: True when a `fp::when` guard failed and stopped the pipe: the receipts end at the guard and NO later step ran. Absent (false) on a full run.

functions.description: Set a value in state

key.description: Identifier for the value within the scope.

value.description: Arbitrary JSON value to store. Replaces any existing value at `scope`/`key`.

old_value.description: The value before the update (None if key didn't exist)

functions.description: Spawn a sub-agent in a child session (direct call only — never a trigger target). Fire-and-forget: returns { child_session_id, child_turn_id } immediately; the child's outcome reaches you only through whatever destination its task names. The child is a LEAF by default (no spawn/send/trigger registration); pass options.orchestrator: true to grant the orchestration surface, still capped by the caller's own policy. The task must include literal values for every required resource selector (for example `db: "primary"`). Omit child `max_turns` unless its budget covers discovery, contract lookup, work, and the deliverable.

AgentMessage.description: The canonical transcript message union. Untagged: the single-variant role tags disambiguate deserialization (assistant/function_result/custom are tried before user so their required fields gate the match).

oneOf.description: Opaque redacted thinking payload — replayed verbatim on the wire.

ExposeMode.description: How allowed functions reach the model (harness.md § Exposure modes).

FunctionPolicy.description: The fail-closed dispatch policy (harness.md § Functions). Absent on the send => every call denied (a plain chat loop).

MessageInput.description: `message` is either a plain string (sugar for a user text message) or a full `AgentMessage`.

Mode.description: Console / send operating mode — prepends a short paragraph before the shared identity prompt. `ask` is also structural: the turn's dispatch policy is capped at the configured default policy, never widened.

OutputContract.description: Free text by default; `json` constrains the final answer to a JSON value, validated against `schema` when supplied.

filesystem_root.description: Absolute filesystem root for the child turn (e.g. an isolated `worktree::create` checkout), written to the child's `metadata.fs_scope.root`. When set it overrides the inherited scope for this child; when absent the child inherits its direct parent's root unchanged.

functions.description: Intersected with the parent policy — narrow, never escalate. An `ask`-mode child is further capped at the configured default policy.

max_children.description: Fan-out guard for the child's own spawns.

max_output_tokens.description: Inherits the parent's ceiling unless explicitly narrowed/overridden.

max_turns.description: Capped at the parent's remaining turn budget. Omit unless a strict child-specific cap is required. It must cover discovery/contract calls plus every work call; very small values (for example 2-3) commonly strand the child before it can produce its deliverable.

max_validation_retries.description: Override the child's validation-retry budget (output contract AND `harness::hook::post-turn` deny re-prompts). Default: worker config.

orchestrator.description: Grant this child the orchestration surface. Default false: a spawned child is a LEAF — its policy gains deny globs for `harness::spawn`, `harness::send`, `engine::register_trigger`, `engine::unregister_trigger` and `engine::registered-triggers::*`, so it performs its assignment and updates shared state without spawning, messaging sessions, or touching trigger registrations. `true` skips those denies; the child still never exceeds its parent's policy.

output.description: The child's deliverable: text / json / json+schema.

system_prompt_strategy.description: How `system_prompt` combines with the built-in prompt: `override` replaces it; `enrich` (default) appends to it; `disabled` omits it.

SystemPromptStrategy.description: How a caller-supplied system prompt combines with the built-in identity prompt.

oneOf.description: Caller prompt replaces the built-in prompt verbatim.
Caller prompt is appended to the built-in identity prompt.
No system prompt is sent to the model.

parent_session_id.description: Display-only parent for the console session tree, used when there is no live parent turn (e.g. a console- or workflow-issued spawn). Writes `SessionMeta.metadata.parent_session_id` so the console nests this child; it does NOT grant policy inheritance or parent-call resolution. Ignored when the dispatcher injects a real parent link (an in-turn spawn).

session_id.description: Spawn into this session, creating it if it does not exist (e.g. a fork, or a pre-chosen id to filter `turn-completed` subscriptions on); default: create fresh. An in-turn spawn may reuse an EXISTING id only inside its own tree (itself, or a child it spawned) — anything else is refused as a cross-run id collision. The response reports `reused: true` on reuse.

task.description: The child's self-contained goal — its opening user message. Include every resolved required selector literally (for example `Use database db: "primary"`); the child cannot infer resources from the parent.

reused.description: The named session already existed and was reused — its prior transcript and parent linkage were retained (only possible with an explicit `session_id`).

I have the contracts for database::execute, database::query, fp::pipe, state::set, harness::spawn.

Now, engine::register_trigger contract — it's documented in the system prompt. The task gives me the exact config structure for the post-turn hook trigger. Let me check what the harness::hook::post-turn trigger type's schema looks like — I should call engine::triggers::info { id: "harness::hook::post-turn" } to get the config schema. Actually, the system prompt says: "engine::triggers::info { id } — that type's config schema and return schema." The task gives a specific config with keys: "sessions", "payload", "result_into", "retry_prompt", "timeout_ms". Let me verify with engine::triggers::info to make sure the config keys are right. That's prudent — the task explicitly says to follow it exactly, and the trigger config must match the schema.

Let me fetch:
- engine::triggers::info { id: "harness::hook::post-turn" }
- engine::triggers::info { id: "state" } — for the wake trigger

Actually, the system prompt documents engine::register_trigger's shapes:
```
engine::register_trigger {
  trigger_type: "state",                    # or cron, timer, or per engine::triggers::list
  config: { scope: "<run>", key: "<key>" }, # that type's own filters
  once: true,                               # TOP-LEVEL, never inside metadata
  # omit function_id to be woken; or name a plain function to call
}
```

So the wake: trigger_type "state", config {scope, key}, label, no function_id. Once — wake defaults to once, but I can explicitly set once: true. The task says "arm TWO once-wakes" — so once: true.

For the validator: trigger_type "harness::hook::post-turn", function_id "fp::pipe", config with sessions, payload (through...), result_into, retry_prompt, timeout_ms. This is the "call a function" shape. The config keys for post-turn hook: "sessions", "payload", "result_into", "retry_prompt", "timeout_ms". Let me verify via engine::triggers::info.

Let me fetch the trigger type schemas. Also engine::triggers::list to confirm available trigger types.

Then Step 1: database::execute twice. I can do that in parallel with the trigger info calls since they're independent.

Let me do:
1. engine::triggers::info { id: "harness::hook::post-turn" }
2. engine::triggers::info { id: "state" }
3. database::execute { db: "primary", sql: "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS msubvtest_bb8e (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, writer TEXT, note TEXT)" }

Wait — database::execute requires "sql" only; db is optional. I'll pass db: "primary" per the task.

Then after CREATE, run DELETE. The task says "twice": first CREATE, then DELETE. They're sequential (DELETE after CREATE). But actually DELETE on a table that doesn't exist would fail — so CREATE must come first. I'll do CREATE and the trigger info in parallel, then DELETE after CREATE succeeds.

Let me proceed.
Contracts fetched. Now let me verify the trigger type schemas and run Step 1 (CREATE TABLE) in parallel.

Step 1 done. Now Step 2 — register TWO validators (one per child), engine::register_trigger with:
- trigger_type: "harness::hook::post-turn"
- function_id: "fp::pipe"
- config: {"sessions": ["<CHILD-N>"], "payload": {"through": [...]}, "result_into": "/value", "retry_prompt": "...", "timeout_ms": 30000}

The config schema for post-turn hook confirms: sessions, payload, result_into, retry_prompt, timeout_ms all valid.

For child 1: sessions: ["e2e_bb8e7dbcfc614c0da2d4d6d7fc76a1c7-child-1"], writer w1 in SQL and state key verdict-w1.
For child 2: sessions: ["e2e_bb8e7dbcfc614c0da2d4d6d7fc76a1c7-child-2"], writer w2.

The through steps:
1. database::query { db: "primary", sql: "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM msubvtest_bb8e WHERE writer = 'wN'" }
2. fp::get { path: "/rows/0/n" }
3. fp::when { op: ">", to: 6 }
4. state::set { scope: "msubv-bb8e", key: "verdict-wN" }

Wait — there's a subtlety. The pipe's threaded value: database::query returns QueryResp { columns, row_count, rows }. The fp::get step gets path "/rows/0/n". Then fp::when checks op ">" to 6. Then state::set with scope/key. But what VALUE does state::set store? The threaded value at that point is the count n (the result of fp::when threads the value through — fp::when passes the value onward if the guard passes, I believe). Actually, fp::when is a guard: it checks the condition, and if passes, the value continues to next step. So state::set receives the count as its threaded value at "/value". The state::set payload has scope and key; the value... hmm.

Wait, the task says: The state::set tail runs ONLY when the guard passes. The payload for state::set in the task: {"scope": "msubv-bb8e", "key": "verdict-wN"} — no explicit value field. state::set requires "value" field per its contract. But in the pipe, the threaded value lands at into (default "/value"). So the state::set step's payload gets the threaded value injected at "/value", i.e., payload.value = count. So the stored value is the count. Good — that matches "each verdict wake carries the accepted row count for one writer."

So state::set receives value = count (the number of rows). The verdict wake payload will carry new_value = count. Good.

Note: the task says config payload should be exactly:
{"through": [{"function": "database::query", "payload": {"db": "primary", "sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM msubvtest_bb8e WHERE writer = 'wN'"}}, {"function": "fp::get", "payload": {"path": "/rows/0/n"}}, {"function": "fp::when", "payload": {"op": ">", "to": 6}}, {"function": "state::set", "payload": {"scope": "msubv-bb8e", "key": "verdict-wN"}}]}

And config: {"sessions": ["<CHILD-N>"], "payload": {...}, "result_into": "/value", "retry_prompt": "...", "timeout_ms": 30000}

details.description: Spawn a sub-agent in a child session (direct call only — never a trigger target). Fire-and-forget: returns { child_session_id, child_turn_id } immediately; the child's outcome reaches you only through whatever destination its task names. The child is a LEAF by default (no spawn/send/trigger registration); pass options.orchestrator: true to grant the orchestration surface, still capped by the caller's own policy. The task must include literal values for every required resource selector (for example `db: "primary"`). Omit child `max_turns` unless its budget covers discovery, contract lookup, work, and the deliverable.

AgentMessage.description: The canonical transcript message union. Untagged: the single-variant role tags disambiguate deserialization (assistant/function_result/custom are tried before user so their required fields gate the match).

oneOf.description: Opaque redacted thinking payload — replayed verbatim on the wire.

ExposeMode.description: How allowed functions reach the model (harness.md § Exposure modes).

FunctionPolicy.description: The fail-closed dispatch policy (harness.md § Functions). Absent on the send => every call denied (a plain chat loop).

MessageInput.description: `message` is either a plain string (sugar for a user text message) or a full `AgentMessage`.

Mode.description: Console / send operating mode — prepends a short paragraph before the shared identity prompt. `ask` is also structural: the turn's dispatch policy is capped at the configured default policy, never widened.

OutputContract.description: Free text by default; `json` constrains the final answer to a JSON value, validated against `schema` when supplied.

filesystem_root.description: Absolute filesystem root for the child turn (e.g. an isolated `worktree::create` checkout), written to the child's `metadata.fs_scope.root`. When set it overrides the inherited scope for this child; when absent the child inherits its direct parent's root unchanged.

functions.description: Intersected with the parent policy — narrow, never escalate. An `ask`-mode child is further capped at the configured default policy.

max_children.description: Fan-out guard for the child's own spawns.

max_output_tokens.description: Inherits the parent's ceiling unless explicitly narrowed/overridden.

max_turns.description: Capped at the parent's remaining turn budget. Omit unless a strict child-specific cap is required. It must cover discovery/contract calls plus every work call; very small values (for example 2-3) commonly strand the child before it can produce its deliverable.

max_validation_retries.description: Override the child's validation-retry budget (output contract AND `harness::hook::post-turn` deny re-prompts). Default: worker config.

orchestrator.description: Grant this child the orchestration surface. Default false: a spawned child is a LEAF — its policy gains deny globs for `harness::spawn`, `harness::send`, `engine::register_trigger`, `engine::unregister_trigger` and `engine::registered-triggers::*`, so it performs its assignment and updates shared state without spawning, messaging sessions, or touching trigger registrations. `true` skips those denies; the child still never exceeds its parent's policy.

output.description: The child's deliverable: text / json / json+schema.

system_prompt_strategy.description: How `system_prompt` combines with the built-in prompt: `override` replaces it; `enrich` (default) appends to it; `disabled` omits it.

SystemPromptStrategy.description: How a caller-supplied system prompt combines with the built-in identity prompt.

oneOf.description: Caller prompt replaces the built-in prompt verbatim.
Caller prompt is appended to the built-in identity prompt.
No system prompt is sent to the model.

parent_session_id.description: Display-only parent for the console session tree, used when there is no live parent turn (e.g. a console- or workflow-issued spawn). Writes `SessionMeta.metadata.parent_session_id` so the console nests this child; it does NOT grant policy inheritance or parent-call resolution. Ignored when the dispatcher injects a real parent link (an in-turn spawn).

session_id.description: Spawn into this session, creating it if it does not exist (e.g. a fork, or a pre-chosen id to filter `turn-completed` subscriptions on); default: create fresh. An in-turn spawn may reuse an EXISTING id only inside its own tree (itself, or a child it spawned) — anything else is refused as a cross-run id collision. The response reports `reused: true` on reuse.

task.description: The child's self-contained goal — its opening user message. Include every resolved required selector literally (for example `Use database db: "primary"`); the child cannot infer resources from the parent.

reused.description: The named session already existed and was reused — its prior transcript and parent linkage were retained (only possible with an explicit `session_id`).

configuration_schema.description: The `config` of a `harness::hook::<point>` trigger binding.

functions.description: pre/post_trigger only: target function_id globs to consult on.

on_error.description: Failure policy (default fail_closed for pre_* and post_turn, fail_open for the other post_*).

payload.description: post_turn only: template mode — send THIS argument object to the bound function instead of the hook envelope, with the turn's parsed result injected at `result_into`. Lets a plain composition function (`fp::pipe`) validate turns without speaking the hook contract; its receipt is read as the verdict (`valid`, or `short_circuited`).

priority.description: Chain order: ascending, ties broken by function_id (default 0).

result_into.description: post_turn template mode: JSON pointer where the result lands in `payload` (default `/value`).

retry_prompt.description: post_turn only: custom corrective prompt sent VERBATIM when this validator denies (replaces the generic "result was not accepted" wrapper). Placeholders: `{value}` = the validator's measured value (fp::pipe receipt `value_preview`), `{reason}` = the deny reason. Validator ERRORS keep the generic text — a task-shaped prompt must not mask a broken validator.

sessions.description: post_turn only: session_id globs this validator gates (omit = all).

configuration_schema.title: HookTriggerConfig

details.description: Synchronous hook: at finalize, after the output contract validated the result, before the turn completes. Deny re-prompts the turn (bounded by max_validation_retries). Config `sessions` globs scope it; config `payload`+`result_into` bind a plain composition function (fp::pipe) as the validator.

content.text:
I have the contracts. Now let me also check the `engine::register_trigger` contract? It's documented in the prompt, but let me confirm what the response looks like — I know from the prompt it returns subscription_id or id. Let me check the docs via `engine::functions::info`? Actually `engine::register_trigger` is an engine function. The system prompt says "The discovery functions are documented here; never introspect them." — `engine::register_trigger` is not a discovery function; it's the trigger registration. It's documented in the prompt. But the instruction says never use a function id from memory — `engine::register_trigger` is given directly in the task and documented in the system prompt, so it's fine.

Let me now proceed:

Step 1 — prepare the table. Two `database::execute` calls:
1. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS msubvtest_0b95 (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, writer TEXT, note TEXT)
2. DELETE FROM msubvtest_0b95

These are dependent (DELETE after CREATE), so must be sequential. Actually they could be considered independent in the sense that DELETE works whether or not table exists... no, if the table doesn't exist, DELETE fails. So CREATE first, then DELETE. Sequential.

Step 2 — register TWO validators (engine::register_trigger), one per child.

For child 1 (session "e2e_0b957531caa04e7c9909f7bf211bea88-child-1", writer w1):
- trigger_type: "harness::hook::post-turn"
- function_id: "fp::pipe"
- config: {"sessions": ["e2e_0b957531caa04e7c9909f7bf211bea88-child-1"], "payload": {"through": [{"function": "database::query", "payload": {"db": "primary", "sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM msubvtest_0b95 WHERE writer = 'w1'"}}, {"function": "fp::get", "payload": {"path": "/rows/0/n"}}, {"function": "fp::when", "payload": {"op": ">", "to": 6}}, {"function": "state::set", "payload": {"scope": "msubv-0b95", "key": "verdict-w1"}}]}, "result_into": "/value", "retry_prompt": "VALIDATOR[w1]: only {value} of the required 7 rows exist for writer w1. Insert exactly 4 more rows with writer w1 into msubvtest_0b95 and reply with a one-line status.", "timeout_ms": 30000}

Wait — the config is the hook trigger config which includes: functions, on_error, payload, priority, result_into, retry_prompt, sessions, timeout_ms. So the config object should be:
{
  "sessions": ["<CHILD-N>"],
  "payload": {"through": [...]},
  "result_into": "/value",
  "retry_prompt": "...",
  "timeout_ms": 30000
}

That matches what the task says: config: {"sessions": [...], "payload": {...}, "result_into": "/value", "retry_prompt": "...", "timeout_ms": 30000}.

The validator pipe: database::query → fp::get /rows/0/n → fp::when op ">" to 6 → state::set. When the count > 6 (i.e., at least 7), the guard passes, and state::set writes verdict-wN. The pipe receipt is read as verdict: `valid` or `short_circuited`. So when the count is ≤ 6, short_circuited → validator denies → retry_prompt sent to child.

Note about `result_into`: the hook's parsed result is injected at `result_into` (default /value). The pipe's first step receives... hmm, with template mode, the payload is sent to the bound function (fp::pipe) with the result injected at result_into. But the pipe's FIRST step receives no threaded value, so this is fine — the first step is database::query.

Wait, actually — does injecting the result at "/value" into the payload interfere? The payload has "through" array. Injecting at "/value" would add "value": <result> to the payload object. fp::pipe payload: {through: [...], value: <hook result>}. fp::pipe only uses "through" and "value" for seeding a leading transform. Since the first step is a producing function (database::query), the value field is ignored. So it's fine.

The `retry_prompt` uses `{value}` placeholder = validator's measured value (fp::pipe receipt value_preview). The value_preview would be... the final step is state::set, which stores the count? Actually state::set's payload is {scope, key} with no value. Hmm, the state::set payload doesn't include a value — it stores... let me think. The pipe threads the transformed value: after fp::when, the value passed to state::set is the count (n). state::set with payload {scope: "msubv-0b95", key: "verdict-w1"} — if no value field is given, what does it store? 

Hmm, actually per the pipe semantics, "the result lands in the next step's payload at `into` (default "/value")". So state::set receives payload = {scope: ..., key: ..., value: <count>}. So it stores the count as the value of verdict-wN. Good — that's what Step 6 needs: "each verdict wake carries the accepted row count for one writer". The state::set value = the count (n from the query). 

And the value_preview of the receipt would be the stored value (the count). So the retry_prompt placeholder {value} = the count measured. Good.

So the state::set payload in the pipe: {"scope": "msubv-0b95", "key": "verdict-w1"} — and the threaded value (the count) gets injected at /value. 

Step 3 — arm TWO once-wakes BEFORE spawning: for each wN, engine::register_trigger with trigger_type "state", config {"scope": "msubv-0b95", "key": "verdict-wN"}, label "wN-validated", and NO function_id. These are "wake me" shape — omit function_id, so the event arrives as a message in THIS session.

Important: the task says arm wakes BEFORE spawning. Also note the binding only sees the future — the children could theoretically finish and write verdicts before the wake is registered? No — wakes are registered before spawning, so events produced after spawn are visible. Good.

Also, per the system prompt, "ALWAYS set one [lifecycle deadline] on any wake your run cannot finish without." The task doesn't mention lifecycle, but says register with trigger_type "state", config {scope, key}, label, no function_id. I'll follow the task exactly. Adding a lifecycle deadline would be prudent... but the task explicitly specifies the exact shape. Hmm. The task says "arm TWO once-wakes BEFORE spawning: for each wN, engine::register_trigger with trigger_type "state", config {"scope": "msubv-0b95", "key": "verdict-wN"}, label "wN-validated", and NO function_id." I could add lifecycle but the task doesn't ask for it, and deviating might be risky. Actually adding a lifecycle wouldn't hurt but the task is precise. I'll keep to spec: trigger_type "state", config {scope, key}, label, once implied (wake defaults to once anyway). The system prompt says explicit once always wins and wake defaults to once. I'll keep the task's exact shape.

Wait — should I include "once": true? The task says "arm TWO once-wakes" — wake shape defaults to once, so omitting is fine. But to be safe and explicit... The task specifies exactly the fields: trigger_type, config, label, no function_id. I'll pass exactly that. Default wake is once.

Step 4 — spawn both children in THIS turn. harness::spawn with session_id <CHILD-N>, task (with wN replaced), options: {"functions": {"allow": ["database::execute"]}, "max_validation_retries": 5}.

Note: the child's policy allows only database::execute. Contract discovery (engine::functions::list / info) is never lost to narrowing per the system prompt. Good. The child task says to call database::execute with db 'primary'. Wait — the child's task: "database::execute, db 'primary', sql \"INSERT INTO msubvtest_0b95 (writer, note) VALUES ('w1','r'),('w1','r'),('w1','r'),('w1','r')\"". The child must pass db: "primary" literally. Good — the task includes the resolved selector.

Hmm, one thing about the child task: it says "Insert exactly 4 rows" but the validator requires count > 6 (at least 7 rows) for the writer. Wait — the validator checks SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE writer = 'w1' > 6. The child inserts exactly 4 rows. So the count after the child's first turn is 4, which is NOT > 6, so the validator denies and sends the retry prompt: "VALIDATOR[w1]: only {value} of the required 7 rows exist for writer w1. Insert exactly 4 more rows with writer w1 into msubvtest_0b95 and reply with a one-line status."

details.description: Subscribe the current harness session to a iii trigger: omit function_id to be notified in this session, or name a non-harness function to call with the event.

BindingTarget.description: What a fire dispatches. `function_id` is any iii function — `harness::send` for a wake or a sub-agent, anything else for a mechanical reaction.

event_into.description: JSON pointer where the event lands inside the payload (default `/event`).

payload.description: Payload template; the fired event is injected into it at `event_into`.

ConditionSpec.description: One declared condition. Evaluated at fire time with the typed decision contract; ordinary iii functions, so a barrier or a claim is just a function someone wrote.

LifecycleRequest.description: The caller-settable half of a binding's lifecycle.

expires_at.description: Wall-clock deadline (epoch ms) after which the binding stops.

max_fires.description: Lifetime delivery budget; the binding retires on its Nth delivery.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. The top-level `once` field remains accepted as shorthand.

request_schema.description: Agent-facing subscription contract.

conditions.description: Gates evaluated at fire time, in order, each an ordinary iii function answering `{ decision: "allow" | "skip", payload?, reason? }`. The built-in safety gates run first and are not listed here.

config.description: The trigger config, passed verbatim to the engine — e.g. `{ "expression": "0 */5 * * * *" }` for cron, or a `state` scope/key.

function_id.description: Target function called on each event. Omit for a notification message into this session — the only shape that can reach you. Any non-harness function your policy allows may be named; `harness::spawn` is NOT a binding target — a binding never starts an agent. Spawn children directly from a turn and register a wake on what they write.

label.description: A short human label echoed back in the notification text.

lifecycle.description: When the binding stops firing. `once` may also be given at the top level (the shorthand every prompt uses).

metadata.description: Call-binding template: `{ payload?, event_into? }`. `payload` is the fixed argument object sent to the target; `event_into` is a JSON pointer naming where the fired event is injected into that payload. Meaningless for a wake; sub-agent fields (task/model/session_id/ options) are rejected — spawning is not something a binding does.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. Defaults by SHAPE: a WAKE (no `function_id`) is once — it parks this session until the event; a CALL binding is STANDING — it runs per matching event until unregistered or its lifecycle ends; `cron` is recurring; `timer` is once. Pass `once` explicitly to override any of these.

target.description: Explicit target, the long form of `function_id` + `metadata`: `{ function_id, payload?, event_into? }`. The shorthands stay valid and mean exactly this.

trigger_type.description: The iii trigger type to listen on: `cron`, `state`, `stream`, `timer` (one-shot deadline: `{ "in_ms": <ms> }` or `{ "at": <epoch ms> }`), or another worker's custom trigger type (e.g. `database::row-changed`). For an ad-hoc signal, subscribe to `state` on a key and have the signaller call `state::set` on it (no dedicated emit needed — the engine fans the trigger out to every subscriber).

functions.description: Run a write statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL).

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Spawn a sub-agent in a child session (direct call only — never a trigger target). The child is a LEAF by default (no spawn/send/trigger registration); pass options.orchestrator: true to grant the orchestration surface, still capped by the caller's own policy. The task must include literal values for every required resource selector (for example `db: "primary"`). Omit child `max_turns` unless its budget covers discovery, contract lookup, work, and the deliverable.

AgentMessage.description: The canonical transcript message union. Untagged: the single-variant role tags disambiguate deserialization (assistant/function_result/custom are tried before user so their required fields gate the match).

oneOf.description: Opaque redacted thinking payload — replayed verbatim on the wire.

ExposeMode.description: How allowed functions reach the model (harness.md § Exposure modes).

FunctionPolicy.description: The fail-closed dispatch policy (harness.md § Functions). Absent on the send => every call denied (a plain chat loop).

MessageInput.description: `message` is either a plain string (sugar for a user text message) or a full `AgentMessage`.

Mode.description: Console / send operating mode — prepends a short paragraph before the shared identity prompt. `ask` is also structural: the turn's dispatch policy is capped at the configured default policy, never widened.

OutputContract.description: Free text by default; `json` constrains the final answer to a JSON value, validated against `schema` when supplied.

filesystem_root.description: Absolute filesystem root for the child turn (e.g. an isolated `worktree::create` checkout), written to the child's `metadata.fs_scope.root`. When set it overrides the inherited scope for this child; when absent the child inherits its direct parent's root unchanged.

functions.description: Intersected with the parent policy — narrow, never escalate. An `ask`-mode child is further capped at the configured default policy.

max_children.description: Fan-out guard for the child's own spawns.

max_output_tokens.description: Inherits the parent's ceiling unless explicitly narrowed/overridden.

max_turns.description: Capped at the parent's remaining turn budget. Omit unless a strict child-specific cap is required. It must cover discovery/contract calls plus every work call; very small values (for example 2-3) commonly strand the child before it can produce its deliverable.

max_validation_retries.description: Override the child's validation-retry budget (output contract AND `harness::hook::post-turn` deny re-prompts). Default: worker config.

orchestrator.description: Grant this child the orchestration surface. Default false: a spawned child is a LEAF — its policy gains deny globs for `harness::spawn`, `harness::send`, `engine::register_trigger`, `engine::unregister_trigger` and `engine::registered-triggers::*`, so it performs its assignment and updates shared state without spawning, messaging sessions, or touching trigger registrations. `true` skips those denies; the child still never exceeds its parent's policy.

output.description: The child's deliverable: text / json / json+schema.

system_prompt_strategy.description: How `system_prompt` combines with the built-in prompt: `override` replaces it; `enrich` (default) appends to it; `disabled` omits it.

SystemPromptStrategy.description: How a caller-supplied system prompt combines with the built-in identity prompt.

oneOf.description: Caller prompt replaces the built-in prompt verbatim.
Caller prompt is appended to the built-in identity prompt.
No system prompt is sent to the model.

parent_session_id.description: Display-only parent for the console session tree, used when there is no live parent turn (e.g. a console- or workflow-issued spawn). Writes `SessionMeta.metadata.parent_session_id` so the console nests this child; it does NOT grant policy inheritance or parent-call resolution. Ignored when the dispatcher injects a real parent link (an in-turn spawn).

session_id.description: Spawn into this session, creating it if it does not exist (e.g. a fork, or a pre-chosen id to filter `turn-completed` subscriptions on); default: create fresh. An in-turn spawn may reuse an EXISTING id only inside its own tree (itself, or a child it spawned) — anything else is refused as a cross-run id collision. The response reports `reused: true` on reuse.

functions.description: Tear down one trigger binding by subscription id: unregister the engine trigger AND delete the durable record (an engine-side unregister alone strands the owner's armed wake). `session_id` must name the binding's owner; in-turn agent calls may omit it (defaults to the calling session). session_id.description: The binding's owner session — a correctness handshake, checked against the record. In-turn agent calls may omit it (the harness injects the calling session). The console's privileged path supplies the owner it just listed.

removed.description: False when no record existed (already retired) — honest, not an error.

functions.description: Run a read-only SQL query and return the result rows.

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

key.description: Identifier for the value within the scope.

value.description: Arbitrary JSON value to store. Replaces any existing value at `scope`/`key`.

old_value.description: The value before the update (None if key didn't exist)

Smallest number in an array (lodash _.min/_.minBy): { value }, or { value, path: "/amount" }. Deviates from lodash _.minBy: returns the NUMBER, not the element holding it, so a fp::when guard can compare it directly. An empty array errors. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Element at index n; negative n counts from the end (lodash _.nth): { value, n: -1 } is the last element. Out of bounds errors naming the length. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Drop top-level keys from an object (lodash _.omit): { value, paths: ["a","b"] }. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Subset an object by top-level keys (lodash _.pick): { value, paths: ["a","b"] } -> {a, b}; missing keys are omitted. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Reverse an array (lodash _.reverse, immutable like lodash/fp): { value }. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Count a collection (lodash _.size): array length, string chars, or object key count: { value }. Non-collections error instead of returning 0. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.

Sort array elements ascending by the value at a JSON pointer (lodash _.sortBy, stable): { value, path } — path "" sorts the elements themselves (primitives). Keys must all be numbers, strings, or booleans; an element missing the path errors. Pair with fp::reverse for descending. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Split a string into an array of strings (lodash _.split): { value, separator: "\n" }. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.

Total an array of numbers (lodash _.sum/_.sumBy): { value }, or { value, path: "/amount" } to pluck the addend from each element first. An empty array totals 0; a non-numeric element errors rather than being skipped. All-integer inputs total to an integer, so the result compares cleanly in a fp::when guard. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Keep the first n elements of an array or the first n characters of a string (lodash _.take): { value, n }. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.
Deduplicate an array, keeping first occurrences (lodash _.uniq): { value }. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.

Guard: test the value at a JSON pointer ({ value, path?, op, to? }; ops ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, exists, not_empty; path defaults to the whole value; a pointer miss FAILS the guard, it never errors). Direct calls return { passed, value }. As a fp::pipe step, a passing guard threads the ORIGINAL value onward unchanged and a failing one STOPS the pipe (`short_circuited: true`), so a trailing write step (e.g. state::set) runs only when the condition holds.

functions.description: Run a write statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL).

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Spawn a sub-agent in a child session (direct call only — never a trigger target). Fire-and-forget: returns { child_session_id, child_turn_id } immediately; the child's outcome reaches you only through whatever destination its task names. The child is a LEAF by default (no spawn/send/trigger registration); pass options.orchestrator: true to grant the orchestration surface, still capped by the caller's own policy. The task must include literal values for every required resource selector (for example `db: "primary"`). Omit child `max_turns` unless its budget covers discovery, contract lookup, work, and the deliverable.

AgentMessage.description: The canonical transcript message union. Untagged: the single-variant role tags disambiguate deserialization (assistant/function_result/custom are tried before user so their required fields gate the match).

oneOf.description: Opaque redacted thinking payload — replayed verbatim on the wire.

ExposeMode.description: How allowed functions reach the model (harness.md § Exposure modes).

FunctionPolicy.description: The fail-closed dispatch policy (harness.md § Functions). Absent on the send => every call denied (a plain chat loop).

MessageInput.description: `message` is either a plain string (sugar for a user text message) or a full `AgentMessage`.

Mode.description: Console / send operating mode — prepends a short paragraph before the shared identity prompt. `ask` is also structural: the turn's dispatch policy is capped at the configured default policy, never widened.

OutputContract.description: Free text by default; `json` constrains the final answer to a JSON value, validated against `schema` when supplied.

filesystem_root.description: Absolute filesystem root for the child turn (e.g. an isolated `worktree::create` checkout), written to the child's `metadata.fs_scope.root`. When set it overrides the inherited scope for this child; when absent the child inherits its direct parent's root unchanged.

functions.description: Intersected with the parent policy — narrow, never escalate. An `ask`-mode child is further capped at the configured default policy.

max_children.description: Fan-out guard for the child's own spawns.

max_output_tokens.description: Inherits the parent's ceiling unless explicitly narrowed/overridden.

max_turns.description: Capped at the parent's remaining turn budget. Omit unless a strict child-specific cap is required. It must cover discovery/contract calls plus every work call; very small values (for example 2-3) commonly strand the child before it can produce its deliverable.

max_validation_retries.description: Override the child's validation-retry budget (output contract AND `harness::hook::post-turn` deny re-prompts). Default: worker config.

orchestrator.description: Grant this child the orchestration surface. Default false: a spawned child is a LEAF — its policy gains deny globs for `harness::spawn`, `harness::send`, `engine::register_trigger`, `engine::unregister_trigger` and `engine::registered-triggers::*`, so it performs its assignment and updates shared state without spawning, messaging sessions, or touching trigger registrations. `true` skips those denies; the child still never exceeds its parent's policy.

output.description: The child's deliverable: text / json / json+schema.

system_prompt_strategy.description: How `system_prompt` combines with the built-in prompt: `override` replaces it; `enrich` (default) appends to it; `disabled` omits it.

SystemPromptStrategy.description: How a caller-supplied system prompt combines with the built-in identity prompt.

oneOf.description: Caller prompt replaces the built-in prompt verbatim.
Caller prompt is appended to the built-in identity prompt.
No system prompt is sent to the model.

parent_session_id.description: Display-only parent for the console session tree, used when there is no live parent turn (e.g. a console- or workflow-issued spawn). Writes `SessionMeta.metadata.parent_session_id` so the console nests this child; it does NOT grant policy inheritance or parent-call resolution. Ignored when the dispatcher injects a real parent link (an in-turn spawn).

session_id.description: Spawn into this session, creating it if it does not exist (e.g. a fork, or a pre-chosen id to filter `turn-completed` subscriptions on); default: create fresh. An in-turn spawn may reuse an EXISTING id only inside its own tree (itself, or a child it spawned) — anything else is refused as a cross-run id collision. The response reports `reused: true` on reuse.

task.description: The child's self-contained goal — its opening user message. Include every resolved required selector literally (for example `Use database db: "primary"`); the child cannot infer resources from the parent.

reused.description: The named session already existed and was reused — its prior transcript and parent linkage were retained (only possible with an explicit `session_id`).

functions.description: Run a short worker-side pipeline in one call: each step triggers a function and its result lands in the next step's payload at `into` (default "/value") — large values flow worker→worker and never enter the chat. fp::* transform steps (get/pick/omit/take/drop/map/filter/split/join/uniq/size/compact/nth/getOr/flatten/sortBy/reverse/when, lodash semantics) run inline and thread the transformed value itself — the {value} wrapper they return when called directly never appears between steps. A failing fp::when guard STOPS the pipe (`short_circuited: true`), so a trailing write step runs only when its condition holds. The FIRST step receives no threaded value: start with a producing function (a fetch, a state::get) or seed a leading transform via payload.value. Example: fetch an article and persist it trimmed: through=[{function:'scrapling::fetch', payload:{url,format:'markdown'}}, {function:'fp::get', payload:{path:'/content'}}, {function:'fp::take', payload:{n:20000}}, {function:'state::set', payload:{scope,key}}]. Returns per-step sizes and a preview, not the value. shell::*/coder::* steps run under the session's harness-stamped filesystem scope; without one (no working directory, or a non-harness caller) they are refused — call them directly instead. Database write steps are refused only while `approval::gate` is registered.

into.description: JSON pointer in THIS step's payload where the previous step's value lands (default `/value`). Object keys only (`~0`/`~1` escapes are decoded); indexing into arrays is unsupported.

payload.description: Base payload for the call.

preview_chars.description: Preview length of the final threaded value in the receipt (capped at 8000).

through.description: Steps run in order; step N+1 receives step N's threaded value.

chars.description: Size of the value threaded OUT of this step (chars of its string or serialized form).

note.description: Set when the threaded value REPLACED a non-null literal already in this step's payload at the `into` pointer — almost always an omitted `into` on a write step clobbering the value it meant to write.

short_circuited.description: True when a `fp::when` guard failed and stopped the pipe: the receipts end at the guard and NO later step ran. Absent (false) on a full run.

functions.description: Run a read-only SQL query and return the result rows.

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Extract the single value at a JSON pointer (lodash _.get): { value, path: "/content" }. A miss names the keys that were available. Mainly useful as a fp::pipe step.

path.description: JSON pointer selecting the value to return (e.g. `/content`).

value.description: Input value (a pipe lands the previous step's value here).

functions.description: Guard: test the value at a JSON pointer ({ value, path?, op, to? }; ops ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, exists, not_empty; path defaults to the whole value; a pointer miss FAILS the guard, it never errors). Direct calls return { passed, value }. As a fp::pipe step, a passing guard threads the ORIGINAL value onward unchanged and a failing one STOPS the pipe (`short_circuited: true`), so a trailing write step (e.g. state::set) runs only when the condition holds.

path.description: JSON pointer selecting what to test (default: the whole value).

to.description: Right-hand side for the comparison ops; meaningless (and rejected) for exists / not_empty.

value.description: Input value (a pipe lands the previous step's value here).
The ORIGINAL input value, untouched — guards test, they never reshape.

value.description: Arbitrary JSON value to store. Replaces any existing value at `scope`/`key`.

old_value.description: The value before the update (None if key didn't exist)

functions.description: Subscribe the current harness session to a iii trigger: omit function_id to be notified in this session, or name a non-harness function to call with the event.

BindingTarget.description: What a fire dispatches. `function_id` is any iii function — `harness::send` for a wake or a sub-agent, anything else for a mechanical reaction.

event_into.description: JSON pointer where the event lands inside the payload (default `/event`).

payload.description: Payload template; the fired event is injected into it at `event_into`.

ConditionSpec.description: One declared condition. Evaluated at fire time with the typed decision contract; ordinary iii functions, so a barrier or a claim is just a function someone wrote.

LifecycleRequest.description: The caller-settable half of a binding's lifecycle.

expires_at.description: Wall-clock deadline (epoch ms) after which the binding stops.

max_fires.description: Lifetime delivery budget; the binding retires on its Nth delivery.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. The top-level `once` field remains accepted as shorthand.

request_schema.description: Agent-facing subscription contract.

conditions.description: Gates evaluated at fire time, in order, each an ordinary iii function answering `{ decision: "allow" | "skip", payload?, reason? }`. The built-in safety gates run first and are not listed here.

config.description: The trigger config, passed verbatim to the engine — e.g. `{ "expression": "0 */5 * * * *" }` for cron, or a `state` scope/key.

function_id.description: Target function called on each event. Omit for a notification message into this session — the only shape that can reach you. Any non-harness function your policy allows may be named; `harness::spawn` is NOT a binding target — a binding never starts an agent. Spawn children directly from a turn and register a wake on what they write.

label.description: A short human label echoed back in the notification text.

lifecycle.description: When the binding stops firing. `once` may also be given at the top level (the shorthand every prompt uses).

metadata.description: Call-binding template: `{ payload?, event_into? }`. `payload` is the fixed argument object sent to the target; `event_into` is a JSON pointer naming where the fired event is injected into that payload. Meaningless for a wake; sub-agent fields (task/model/session_id/ options) are rejected — spawning is not something a binding does.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. Defaults by SHAPE: a WAKE (no `function_id`) is once — it parks this session until the event; a CALL binding is STANDING — it runs per matching event until unregistered or its lifecycle ends; `cron` is recurring; `timer` is once. Pass `once` explicitly to override any of these.

target.description: Explicit target, the long form of `function_id` + `metadata`: `{ function_id, payload?, event_into? }`. The shorthands stay valid and mean exactly this.

trigger_type.description: The iii trigger type to listen on: `cron`, `state`, `stream`, `timer` (one-shot deadline: `{ "in_ms": <ms> }` or `{ "at": <epoch ms> }`), or another worker's custom trigger type (e.g. `database::row-changed`). For an ad-hoc signal, subscribe to `state` on a key and have the signaller call `state::set` on it (no dedicated emit needed — the engine fans the trigger out to every subscriber).

id.description: The id of the registered trigger; pass to `engine::unregister_trigger`.

functions.description: Run a write statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL).

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Run a read-only SQL query and return the result rows.

db.description: Logical database name. Optional — omitting it targets the sole configured database, or `primary` when several are configured.

functions.description: Run a short worker-side pipeline in one call: each step triggers a function and its result lands in the next step's payload at `into` (default "/value") — large values flow worker→worker and never enter the chat. fp::* transform steps (get/pick/omit/take/drop/map/filter/split/join/uniq/size/compact/nth/getOr/flatten/sortBy/reverse/when, lodash semantics) run inline and thread the transformed value itself — the {value} wrapper they return when called directly never appears between steps. A failing fp::when guard STOPS the pipe (`short_circuited: true`), so a trailing write step runs only when its condition holds. The FIRST step receives no threaded value: start with a producing function (a fetch, a state::get) or seed a leading transform via payload.value. Example: fetch an article and persist it trimmed: through=[{function:'scrapling::fetch', payload:{url,format:'markdown'}}, {function:'fp::get', payload:{path:'/content'}}, {function:'fp::take', payload:{n:20000}}, {function:'state::set', payload:{scope,key}}]. Returns per-step sizes and a preview, not the value. shell::*/coder::* steps run under the session's harness-stamped filesystem scope; without one (no working directory, or a non-harness caller) they are refused — call them directly instead. Database write steps are refused only while `approval::gate` is registered.

into.description: JSON pointer in THIS step's payload where the previous step's value lands (default `/value`). Object keys only (`~0`/`~1` escapes are decoded); indexing into arrays is unsupported.

payload.description: Base payload for the call.

preview_chars.description: Preview length of the final threaded value in the receipt (capped at 8000).

through.description: Steps run in order; step N+1 receives step N's threaded value.

chars.description: Size of the value threaded OUT of this step (chars of its string or serialized form).

note.description: Set when the threaded value REPLACED a non-null literal already in this step's payload at the `into` pointer — almost always an omitted `into` on a write step clobbering the value it meant to write.

short_circuited.description: True when a `fp::when` guard failed and stopped the pipe: the receipts end at the guard and NO later step ran. Absent (false) on a full run.

functions.description: Set a value in state

key.description: Identifier for the value within the scope.

value.description: Arbitrary JSON value to store. Replaces any existing value at `scope`/`key`.

old_value.description: The value before the update (None if key didn't exist)

functions.description: Spawn a sub-agent in a child session (direct call only — never a trigger target). Fire-and-forget: returns { child_session_id, child_turn_id } immediately; the child's outcome reaches you only through whatever destination its task names. The child is a LEAF by default (no spawn/send/trigger registration); pass options.orchestrator: true to grant the orchestration surface, still capped by the caller's own policy. The task must include literal values for every required resource selector (for example `db: "primary"`). Omit child `max_turns` unless its budget covers discovery, contract lookup, work, and the deliverable.

AgentMessage.description: The canonical transcript message union. Untagged: the single-variant role tags disambiguate deserialization (assistant/function_result/custom are tried before user so their required fields gate the match).

oneOf.description: Opaque redacted thinking payload — replayed verbatim on the wire.

ExposeMode.description: How allowed functions reach the model (harness.md § Exposure modes).

FunctionPolicy.description: The fail-closed dispatch policy (harness.md § Functions). Absent on the send => every call denied (a plain chat loop).

MessageInput.description: `message` is either a plain string (sugar for a user text message) or a full `AgentMessage`.

Mode.description: Console / send operating mode — prepends a short paragraph before the shared identity prompt. `ask` is also structural: the turn's dispatch policy is capped at the configured default policy, never widened.

OutputContract.description: Free text by default; `json` constrains the final answer to a JSON value, validated against `schema` when supplied.

filesystem_root.description: Absolute filesystem root for the child turn (e.g. an isolated `worktree::create` checkout), written to the child's `metadata.fs_scope.root`. When set it overrides the inherited scope for this child; when absent the child inherits its direct parent's root unchanged.

functions.description: Intersected with the parent policy — narrow, never escalate. An `ask`-mode child is further capped at the configured default policy.

max_children.description: Fan-out guard for the child's own spawns.

max_output_tokens.description: Inherits the parent's ceiling unless explicitly narrowed/overridden.

max_turns.description: Capped at the parent's remaining turn budget. Omit unless a strict child-specific cap is required. It must cover discovery/contract calls plus every work call; very small values (for example 2-3) commonly strand the child before it can produce its deliverable.

max_validation_retries.description: Override the child's validation-retry budget (output contract AND `harness::hook::post-turn` deny re-prompts). Default: worker config.

orchestrator.description: Grant this child the orchestration surface. Default false: a spawned child is a LEAF — its policy gains deny globs for `harness::spawn`, `harness::send`, `engine::register_trigger`, `engine::unregister_trigger` and `engine::registered-triggers::*`, so it performs its assignment and updates shared state without spawning, messaging sessions, or touching trigger registrations. `true` skips those denies; the child still never exceeds its parent's policy.

output.description: The child's deliverable: text / json / json+schema.

system_prompt_strategy.description: How `system_prompt` combines with the built-in prompt: `override` replaces it; `enrich` (default) appends to it; `disabled` omits it.

SystemPromptStrategy.description: How a caller-supplied system prompt combines with the built-in identity prompt.

oneOf.description: Caller prompt replaces the built-in prompt verbatim.
Caller prompt is appended to the built-in identity prompt.
No system prompt is sent to the model.

parent_session_id.description: Display-only parent for the console session tree, used when there is no live parent turn (e.g. a console- or workflow-issued spawn). Writes `SessionMeta.metadata.parent_session_id` so the console nests this child; it does NOT grant policy inheritance or parent-call resolution. Ignored when the dispatcher injects a real parent link (an in-turn spawn).

session_id.description: Spawn into this session, creating it if it does not exist (e.g. a fork, or a pre-chosen id to filter `turn-completed` subscriptions on); default: create fresh. An in-turn spawn may reuse an EXISTING id only inside its own tree (itself, or a child it spawned) — anything else is refused as a cross-run id collision. The response reports `reused: true` on reuse.

task.description: The child's self-contained goal — its opening user message. Include every resolved required selector literally (for example `Use database db: "primary"`); the child cannot infer resources from the parent.

reused.description: The named session already existed and was reused — its prior transcript and parent linkage were retained (only possible with an explicit `session_id`).

content.text:
Now I have the contracts. Let me proceed with the steps.

Step 1 — prepare the goal table. Call database::execute (db "primary") twice:
1. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fsubvtest_7434 (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, note TEXT)`
2. `DELETE FROM fsubvtest_7434`

The request schema for database::execute: required ["sql"], optional db, params, returning. So payload: { db: "primary", sql: "..." }.

These two calls are sequential? They could be done in parallel actually — the CREATE and DELETE are independent in that order doesn't matter much, but DELETE after CREATE makes sense. Actually they could both run in parallel since CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS will create, and DELETE will delete rows. But if DELETE runs before CREATE... it would fail with no such table. So they must be sequential: CREATE first, then DELETE. Let me do them in order.

Actually, to be safe, do them sequentially. Let me do the first call.

Step 2 — install the child's validator. engine::register_trigger with:
- trigger_type: "harness::hook::post-turn"
- function_id: "fp::pipe"
- config: {"sessions": ["e2e_74342dc0b9a449f69d3c60f22c527a84-child-1"], "payload": {"through": [...]}, "result_into": "/value", "retry_prompt": "...", "timeout_ms": 30000}

The config schema for harness::hook::post-turn: sessions (array of strings), payload (object), result_into (string), retry_prompt (string), timeout_ms (uint64), on_error, priority, functions. additionalProperties: false. So config keys must be exactly these. The given config uses sessions, payload, result_into, retry_prompt, timeout_ms — all valid.

The engine::register_trigger call shape from the system prompt:
```
engine::register_trigger {
  trigger_type: "harness::hook::post-turn",
  function_id: "fp::pipe",
  config: {...},
  # once? For the validator... the prompt didn't mention once. Default for a call binding is standing. Actually, for a post-turn hook validator, we want it standing (it validates every turn of the child). The instructions don't specify once for Step 2, so we omit it — default standing.
}
```

Wait — the instruction says the response echoes effective value. The system prompt says "Defaults when you omit once: a wake is once, a call is standing". So for the validator (a call binding with function_id), omitting once → standing. Good, that's what we want: it validates each turn of the child.

I need to remember the subscription_id returned.

Step 3 — arm wake BEFORE spawning, WITH a deadline:
```
engine::register_trigger {
  trigger_type: "state",
  config: {"scope": "fsubv-7434", "key": "verdict"},
  label: "child-validated",
  lifecycle: {"expires_at": 1786431605158},
  # NO function_id → wake me
}
```
The system prompt shows wake shape: omit function_id, event arrives as message in this session. `once: true` is default for a wake (default wake is once). I can omit once or set it. The instructions say "arm your wake ... with a deadline ... and NO function_id". It doesn't mention once. Default wake is once. I'll omit once (default once). Actually to be safe and explicit, I could set once: true. The instruction says "with a deadline" and "NO function_id". It doesn't say once, but the default is once for wakes. I'll include lifecycle with expires_at only, and maybe once: true explicitly. The instructions in step 3: `engine::register_trigger with trigger_type "state", config {"scope": "fsubv-7434", "key": "verdict"}, label "child-validated", lifecycle: {"expires_at": 1786431605158}, and NO function_id.` So include exactly those: trigger_type, config, label, lifecycle. Once defaults to true for wake. Fine.

Order: Step 2 (validator) then Step 3 (wake) then Step 4 (spawn). Step 3 must be BEFORE spawn (Step 4). Step 2 also before spawn (validator must be installed before the child's turns). All three must be in order: 2, 3, 4. Steps 1 is the DB prep.

Can I do step 1 calls and step 2/3 in parallel? Step 1's two calls must be sequential (CREATE then DELETE). Steps 2 and 3 are independent of step 1 and of each other. But the instructions say follow the steps exactly in order. There's a dependency: the child's validator checks the count in table fsubvtest_7434, which must exist (created in step 1). The validator binding is installed in step 2, but the pipe runs only when the child posts a turn, so table must exist by then. The wake (step 3) must be armed before spawn (step 4). The spawn (step 4) should be after step 3.

I could run CREATE first, then in parallel DELETE + register validator + register wake, then spawn. But to follow steps exactly and avoid races, let me do them in order but batch where independent.

Let me do:
1. Call 1: database::execute CREATE TABLE.
2. Then in parallel: database::execute DELETE, engine::register_trigger (validator), engine::register_trigger (wake)? Hmm, but the steps say Step 2 then Step 3. The validator and wake are independent of each other, so they can be batched together after DELETE. Actually the DELETE is independent of the registrations too. So after CREATE succeeds, I can batch: DELETE, validator registration, wake registration. Then spawn.

Actually wait — is there any dependency between DELETE and the validator? No. The validator only runs when child posts turns (after spawn). Wake only fires on state write of verdict. So batching DELETE + both registrations in one block is fine.

But hmm, the instructions say "Follow the steps exactly." Step order: 1 (two DB calls), 2 (validator), 3 (wake), 4 (spawn). I'll keep the ordering but batch where safe. Let me be a bit conservative: run CREATE, then run DELETE + validator + wake in parallel (all independent, after CREATE), then spawn.

Actually, strictly: Step 1 requires the two executes. Then step 2 register validator. Then step 3 register wake. Then step 4 spawn. Batching DELETE with the registrations doesn't violate anything since DELETE is part of step 1 and doesn't depend on the registrations. But to "follow steps exactly", maybe do CREATE → DELETE → validator → wake → spawn, batching only truly independent calls. The two register_trigger calls are independent of each other and of DELETE, so one parallel block with all three is fine and safe.

Hmm, but there's a subtle point about engine::register_trigger for the validator: does it need the function_id "fp::pipe" to be callable? Yes, function_id must be a plain function my policy allows. fp::pipe is allowed.

config.description: The trigger config, passed verbatim to the engine — e.g. `{ "expression": "0 */5 * * * *" }` for cron, or a `state` scope/key.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. details.description: Subscribe the current harness session to a iii trigger: omit function_id to be notified in this session, or name a non-harness function to call with the event.

BindingTarget.description: What a fire dispatches. `function_id` is any iii function — `harness::send` for a wake or a sub-agent, anything else for a mechanical reaction.

event_into.description: JSON pointer where the event lands inside the payload (default `/event`).

payload.description: Payload template; the fired event is injected into it at `event_into`.

ConditionSpec.description: One declared condition. Evaluated at fire time with the typed decision contract; ordinary iii functions, so a barrier or a claim is just a function someone wrote.

LifecycleRequest.description: The caller-settable half of a binding's lifecycle.

expires_at.description: Wall-clock deadline (epoch ms) after which the binding stops.

max_fires.description: Lifetime delivery budget; the binding retires on its Nth delivery.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. The top-level `once` field remains accepted as shorthand.

request_schema.description: Agent-facing subscription contract.

conditions.description: Gates evaluated at fire time, in order, each an ordinary iii function answering `{ decision: "allow" | "skip", payload?, reason? }`. The built-in safety gates run first and are not listed here.

config.description: The trigger config, passed verbatim to the engine — e.g. `{ "expression": "0 */5 * * * *" }` for cron, or a `state` scope/key.

function_id.description: Target function called on each event. Omit for a notification message into this session — the only shape that can reach you. Any non-harness function your policy allows may be named; `harness::spawn` is NOT a binding target — a binding never starts an agent. Spawn children directly from a turn and register a wake on what they write.

label.description: A short human label echoed back in the notification text.

lifecycle.description: When the binding stops firing. `once` may also be given at the top level (the shorthand every prompt uses).

metadata.description: Call-binding template: `{ payload?, event_into? }`. `payload` is the fixed argument object sent to the target; `event_into` is a JSON pointer naming where the fired event is injected into that payload. Meaningless for a wake; sub-agent fields (task/model/session_id/ options) are rejected — spawning is not something a binding does.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. Defaults by SHAPE: a WAKE (no `function_id`) is once — it parks this session until the event; a CALL binding is STANDING — it runs per matching event until unregistered or its lifecycle ends; `cron` is recurring; `timer` is once. Pass `once` explicitly to override any of these.

target.description: Explicit target, the long form of `function_id` + `metadata`: `{ function_id, payload?, event_into? }`. The shorthands stay valid and mean exactly this.

trigger_type.description: The iii trigger type to listen on: `cron`, `state`, `stream`, `timer` (one-shot deadline: `{ "in_ms": <ms> }` or `{ "at": <epoch ms> }`), or another worker's custom trigger type (e.g. `database::row-changed`). functions.description: Subscribe the current harness session to a iii trigger: omit function_id to be notified in this session, or name a non-harness function to call with the event.

BindingTarget.description: What a fire dispatches. `function_id` is any iii function — `harness::send` for a wake or a sub-agent, anything else for a mechanical reaction.

event_into.description: JSON pointer where the event lands inside the payload (default `/event`).

payload.description: Payload template; the fired event is injected into it at `event_into`.

ConditionSpec.description: One declared condition. Evaluated at fire time with the typed decision contract; ordinary iii functions, so a barrier or a claim is just a function someone wrote.

LifecycleRequest.description: The caller-settable half of a binding's lifecycle.

expires_at.description: Wall-clock deadline (epoch ms) after which the binding stops.

max_fires.description: Lifetime delivery budget; the binding retires on its Nth delivery.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. The top-level `once` field remains accepted as shorthand.

request_schema.description: Agent-facing subscription contract.

conditions.description: Gates evaluated at fire time, in order, each an ordinary iii function answering `{ decision: "allow" | "skip", payload?, reason? }`. The built-in safety gates run first and are not listed here.

config.description: The trigger config, passed verbatim to the engine — e.g. `{ "expression": "0 */5 * * * *" }` for cron, or a `state` scope/key.

function_id.description: Target function called on each event. Omit for a notification message into this session — the only shape that can reach you. Any non-harness function your policy allows may be named; `harness::spawn` is NOT a binding target — a binding never starts an agent. Spawn children directly from a turn and register a wake on what they write.

label.description: A short human label echoed back in the notification text.

lifecycle.description: When the binding stops firing. `once` may also be given at the top level (the shorthand every prompt uses).

metadata.description: Call-binding template: `{ payload?, event_into? }`. `payload` is the fixed argument object sent to the target; `event_into` is a JSON pointer naming where the fired event is injected into that payload. Meaningless for a wake; sub-agent fields (task/model/session_id/ options) are rejected — spawning is not something a binding does.

once.description: Auto-unsubscribe after the first delivered fire. Defaults by SHAPE: a WAKE (no `function_id`) is once — it parks this session until the event; a CALL binding is STANDING — it runs per matching event until unregistered or its lifecycle ends; `cron` is recurring; `timer` is once. Pass `once` explicitly to override any of these.

target.description: Explicit target, the long form of `function_id` + `metadata`: `{ function_id, payload?, event_into? }`. The shorthands stay valid and mean exactly this.

trigger_type.description: The iii trigger type to listen on: `cron`, `state`, `stream`, `timer` (one-shot deadline: `{ "in_ms": <ms> }` or `{ "at": <epoch ms> }`), or another worker's custom trigger type (e.g. `database::row-changed`). For an ad-hoc signal, subscribe to `state` on a key and have the signaller call `state::set` on it (no dedicated emit needed — the engine fans the trigger out to every subscriber).

Internal provider for TriggerAction::Enqueue

Trigger-binding guard: compare a JSON pointer inside the fired event and answer the condition contract ({ decision: "allow" | "skip", reason }). Config is { path?, op, to?, negate? } with the fp::when ops (==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, exists, not_empty); a pointer that resolves to nothing SKIPS rather than erroring, so "not there yet" is an ordinary answer. Use it as a binding's `conditions` entry so a reaction fires only on events that matter — it is not a fan-in gate (that is state::barrier), it filters one event at a time.

Run a short worker-side pipeline in one call: each step triggers a function and its result lands in the next step's payload at `into` (default "/value") — large values flow worker→worker and never enter the chat. fp::* transform steps (get/pick/omit/take/drop/map/filter/split/join/uniq/size/compact/nth/getOr/flatten/sortBy/reverse/when, lodash semantics) run inline and thread the transformed value itself — the {value} wrapper they return when called directly never appears between steps. A failing fp::when guard STOPS the pipe (`short_circuited: true`), so a trailing write step runs only when its condition holds. The FIRST step receives no threaded value: start with a producing function (a fetch, a state::get) or seed a leading transform via payload.value. Example: fetch an article and persist it trimmed: through=[{function:'scrapling::fetch', payload:{url,format:'markdown'}}, {function:'fp::get', payload:{path:'/content'}}, {function:'fp::take', payload:{n:20000}}, {function:'state::set', payload:{scope,key}}]. Returns per-step sizes and a preview, not the value. shell::*/coder::* steps run under the session's harness-stamped filesystem scope; without one (no working directory, or a non-harness caller) they are refused — call them directly instead. Database write steps are refused only while `approval::gate` is registered.

Spawn a sub-agent in a child session (direct call only — never a trigger target). Fire-and-forget: returns { child_session_id, child_turn_id } immediately; the child's outcome reaches you only through whatever destination its task names. The child is a LEAF by default (no spawn/send/trigger registration); pass options.orchestrator: true to grant the orchestration surface, still capped by the caller's own policy. The task must include literal values for every required resource selector (for example `db: "primary"`). Omit child `max_turns` unless its budget covers discovery, contract lookup, work, and the deliverable.

Reserve a PRIVATE state namespace for the calling worker: its scopes become invisible to public state::* and to trigger fan-out, and internal accessors `<functions_prefix>::state::{get, list, compare-and-set}` are registered. A worker may only claim the namespace matching its own worker name (engine-stamped caller identity). Idempotent; claims survive a state restart.
